findings.claim: Beneficiary had a qualifying prior hospital stay for a condition later treated in the SNF
findings.quote: rendered for a condition for which the patient received inpatient hospital services
findings.case_fact: D.E. had a prior hospital stay for a diagnosis of congestive heart failure from August 23, 2009, to August 26, 2009.

findings.claim: Skilled rehabilitation (PT) services are the type of care the SNF benefit covers
findings.quote: The patient requires skilled nursing services or skilled rehabilitation services
findings.case_fact: D.E. was referred to PT due to decreased strength and decreased ADLs due to illness.

findings.claim: Skilled observation and assessment of fluctuating vital signs is a covered type of SNF skilled service
findings.quote: Observation and assessment are skilled services when the likelihood of change in a patient’s condition requires skilled nursing
findings.case_fact: On at least thirteen occasions the beneficiary’s medications had to be adjusted due to fluctuations in his blood pressure and heart rate.

findings.claim: Skilled nursing observation leading to treatment changes is a covered home health service
findings.quote: there is a reasonable potential that skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary’s insulin dosage was adjusted numerous times during this period

findings.claim: Skilled observation and assessment after hospitalization is a covered type of SNF service
findings.quote: Observation and assessment are skilled services when the likelihood of change in a patient’s condition requires skilled nursing
findings.case_fact: a physician indicated that the beneficiary required skilled nursing for one week to monitor for signs of fever

findings.claim: Skilled monitoring after surgery on transfer to a SNF is reasonable and necessary
findings.quote: Skilled observation and monitoring of the patient for possible adverse reaction to the operative procedure
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary’s hospitalization from February 12 to February 17, 2010, for “worsening gross hematuria.”

findings.claim: Skilled PT is a covered type of SNF care, but the facts do not show it was for a condition treated in a qualifying hospital stay (UNKNOWN)
findings.quote: rendered for a condition for which the patient received inpatient hospital services
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary sustained a fall in the facility on September 2, 2008, resulting in a “left upper extremity sprain,”

findings.claim: Skilled PT must follow an active written treatment plan; the facts do not settle this (UNKNOWN)
findings.quote: The services must be directly and specifically related to an active written treatment plan
findings.case_fact: The appellant asserts that the beneficiary made steady progress throughout physical therapy

findings.claim: Skilled PT teaching safe stair/transfer technique is a covered home health therapy service
findings.quote: Physical therapy would be reasonable and necessary to teach the patient to climb and descend stairs safely.
findings.case_fact: the skilled therapist was needed to teach the beneficiary how to safely transfer to and from the lift.

findings.claim: Skilled therapy for a maintenance program is covered; homebound status is UNKNOWN
findings.quote: skilled therapy services are covered when an individualized assessment of the patient’s clinical condition demonstrates
findings.case_fact: the therapist was “in the process of designing an appropriate home exercise program”

findings.claim: Skilled nursing teaching/reinforcement of ostomy care is a covered service
findings.quote: Teaching care for a recent ostomy or where reinforcement of ostomy care is needed
findings.case_fact: His bowel and bladder functions are maintained by colostomy and urostomy.

findings.claim: Skilled nursing care of fistulas is a covered skilled service
findings.quote: Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary developed a fistula near the colostomy site.

findings.claim: Home health coverage requires meeting qualifying criteria; the facts say nothing about the beneficiary meeting them (UNKNOWN)
findings.quote: For any home health services to be covered by Medicare, the patient must meet the qualifying criteria as specified in §30
findings.case_fact: the appellant asserts that coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis

findings.claim: Part-time or intermittent aide and nursing services are a covered type; only an appellant assertion is given
findings.quote: Medicare covers either part-time or intermittent home health aide services or skilled nursing services
findings.case_fact: coverage is available for home health aide or skilled nursing services on a part-time basis

findings.claim: IRF care is covered only if specific requirements are met; the facts give no clinical or patient-status information (UNKNOWN)
findings.quote: IRF care is only considered by Medicare to be reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: This appeal involves IRF services provided by the appellant to five beneficiaries on various dates between March 2003 and May 2004.

findings.claim: IRF rehabilitation after acute hospital surgery is the type of care the IRF benefit covers
findings.quote: The inpatient rehabilitation facility (IRF) benefit is designed to provide intensive rehabilitation therapy
findings.case_fact: the beneficiary was transferred and admitted to the appellant’s IRF where she received treatment and rehabilitation services

findings.claim: Ability to actively participate in intensive therapy is not settled (UNKNOWN)
findings.quote: patients must be able to actively participate in and benefit from the intensive rehabilitation therapy program
findings.case_fact: experienced severe pain requiring multiple treatments including Norco and patient controlled administration of Dilaudid.
